# Organisation file reference

<!-- Generated by `npm run packs:docs` in sc-gateway from the organisation schema. Do not edit by hand. -->

This page explains every key of an organisation file and every value you can choose.
It is the page to keep open while you write your file.

One organisation is one file: `<country>/organisations/<primary-domain>.yaml`, for example `fi/organisations/esimerkkikauppa.example.yaml`.
The file name is the organisation's id, and it never changes.
For a new organisation, the id is the organisation's main domain, the first one in your `domains` list.

In VS Code, the recommended YAML extension shows these descriptions as you type: hover over a key, or press Ctrl+Space to see the allowed values.

## Example

```yaml
# fi/organisations/esimerkkikauppa.example.yaml
name: Esimerkkikauppa
category: retail
domains:
  - domain: esimerkkikauppa.example # the first domain is the main one
    evidence: https://www.esimerkkikauppa.example/ # a page that shows the domain is theirs
    checked: 2026-11-12 # the day you looked at that page
    says: Esimerkkikauppa's own website # what the page shows
aliases: # other names people use for the organisation
  - Esimerkkikauppa Oy
reportTo: # where the organisation wants scam reports
  - email: abuse@esimerkkikauppa.example
    evidence: https://www.esimerkkikauppa.example/turvallisuus/huijaukset
    checked: 2026-11-12
    says: Security page asks customers to report scams to this address
```

## How evidence works

Every domain and every reporting address needs proof: a public web page that shows it.
Write the link in `evidence`, the day you looked at the page in `checked`, and what the page shows in `says`.

If two entries use the same page, write `checked` and `says` once. The other entry only needs the same `evidence` link.
If you write them twice with different content, the check stops and shows both lines.

Passing the automatic check does not make your entry trusted.
After the data is released, phish.fi opens your pages again and looks for the domain or address on them.

## Keys you write

`Needed: Once per page` means you write it on one entry for each page.

| Key | Needed | If you leave it out | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | Yes | - | The organisation's name as people know it. It is also matched as a name in messages. |
| `category` | Yes | - | What kind of organisation this is. phish.fi groups organisations by it (it sets the organisation's sector); it does not change which names or domains match. |
| `domains[]` | Yes, at least one | - | The organisation's own web domains, each with evidence. The first is the primary domain; a new organisation's file is named after it. |
| `domains[].domain` | Yes | - | A registrable domain of the organisation, in lower case, without www, https:// or a path (for example esimerkkikauppa.example). |
| `domains[].relationship` | No | `owned` | How the domain relates to the organisation. Default: owned. |
| `domains[].evidence` | Yes | - | Link (https://...) to a public page that proves this entry. For a domain: a page showing the domain belongs to the organisation. For a reporting address: a page of the organisation that shows this address and asks people to send scam reports there. Required. phish.fi opens the page after release and looks for the domain or address on it. |
| `domains[].checked` | Once per page | - | The date you looked at the evidence page, written as YYYY-MM-DD. Needed once per page: when several entries cite the same page, write it on one of them. |
| `domains[].says` | Once per page | - | What the evidence page shows, in a sentence of your own words (no email addresses). Needed once per page, like checked. |
| `domains[].evidenceKind` | No | `official_site` | What kind of page the evidence is. Default: official_site. A reporting address can only use official_site or organisation_statement; official_register is for domains. |
| `aliases[]` | No | The organisation's name is added for you | Other names messages may use for the organisation. Write each as plain text, or as an object with value, kind, match and weight. The organisation's name is added automatically. |
| `aliases[].value` | Yes, in this form | - | Another name messages may use for the organisation. |
| `aliases[].kind` | No | - | What kind of name this is. Optional. |
| `aliases[].match` | No | `token_exact` | How the name is matched. Default: token_exact. |
| `aliases[].weight` | No | `low` for names of 4 characters or fewer, otherwise `medium` | How strongly the name alone points to the organisation. Default: low for names of 4 characters or fewer, otherwise medium. |
| `reportTo[]` | Yes, for a new organisation | - | Email addresses where the organisation asks people to report phishing that imitates it. A new organisation needs at least one. |
| `reportTo[].email` | Yes | - | The reporting address exactly as the organisation's page shows it. It must be on one of the organisation's owned or authorized domains. |
| `reportTo[].evidence` | Yes | - | Link (https://...) to a public page that proves this entry. For a domain: a page showing the domain belongs to the organisation. For a reporting address: a page of the organisation that shows this address and asks people to send scam reports there. Required. phish.fi opens the page after release and looks for the domain or address on it. |
| `reportTo[].checked` | Once per page | - | The date you looked at the evidence page, written as YYYY-MM-DD. Needed once per page: when several entries cite the same page, write it on one of them. |
| `reportTo[].says` | Once per page | - | What the evidence page shows, in a sentence of your own words (no email addresses). Needed once per page, like checked. |
| `reportTo[].evidenceKind` | No | `official_site` | What kind of page the evidence is. Default: official_site. A reporting address can only use official_site or organisation_statement; official_register is for domains. |
| `reportTo[].threatCategories[]` | No | `[phishing]` | What kinds of attack this address takes reports about. phish.fi sends a report here only when the report has one of these categories. Default: [phishing]. |
| `reportTo[].payload` | No | `structured_only` | Whether reports sent here include the original message. Default: structured_only. |
| `reportTo[].acceptsAutomatedReports` | No | `false` | true when the organisation's page says it accepts reports sent by automated services. It is recorded with the address and does not by itself make phish.fi send anything automatically. Default: false. |
| `reportTo[].name` | No | `<name> phishing reports` | A display name for the address, shown to the person reporting. Default: "<organisation name> phishing reports". |
| `threatCategories[]` | No | - | Threat categories typical of attacks that imitate this organisation. Optional. |
| `organisationType` | No | - | Optional. The organisation's legal or institutional type. Descriptive only: it does not change matching or routing. |
| `sector` | No | - | Optional. The organisation's main industry sector. Descriptive only: it does not change matching or routing. |
| `additionalSectors[]` | No | - | Optional. Up to 4 further sectors, same values as sector. Needs sector. Descriptive only. |

## Values you can choose

### category

Used by `category`.

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `bank` | A bank or other credit institution. |
| `identification_broker` | A service that relays strong electronic identification to other services. |
| `payment_provider` | A payment service, such as a payment app, payment processor or parking payment service. |
| `card_issuer` | A payment card issuer or card network. |
| `government_service` | A government agency or public service. |
| `logistics` | A postal, parcel or delivery company. |
| `telecom` | A mobile, broadband or other telecom operator. |
| `email_provider` | An email or webmail provider. |
| `crypto_service` | A cryptocurrency exchange or wallet service. |
| `marketplace` | An online marketplace where others sell. |
| `retail` | A shop or online store. |
| `other` | Anything else. |

### Threat categories

Used by `threatCategories` (organisation) and `reportTo[].threatCategories`.

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `phishing` | The general category: tricking people into giving away credentials, codes, card details or personal data. |
| `credential_theft` | Stealing login credentials. |
| `credential_theft.online_banking` | Stealing online banking credentials. |
| `credential_theft.email_account` | Stealing email account credentials. |
| `credential_theft.national_eid` | Stealing national electronic identification credentials. |
| `authentication_abuse` | Misusing strong sign-in: getting the victim to hand over a one-time code or approve a sign-in. |
| `authentication_abuse.code_theft` | Getting the victim to hand over a one-time or verification code. |
| `authentication_abuse.approval` | Getting the victim to approve a sign-in or payment in an app. |
| `payment_card_theft` | Stealing payment card details. |
| `personal_data_theft` | Stealing personal data such as identity numbers or addresses. |
| `brand_impersonation` | Pretending to be the organisation, whatever the goal. |
| `payment_fraud` | Tricking people into paying money. |
| `payment_fraud.invoice` | Fake or altered invoices. |
| `payment_fraud.advance_fee` | Asking for a small payment up front to release something larger. |
| `malware_delivery` | Getting people to install malware or open a malicious file. |

### relationship

Used by `domains[].relationship`.

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `owned` | The organisation owns the domain and uses it itself. |
| `authorized` | Someone else runs the domain for the organisation, with its permission (for example a service provider). |
| `associated` | Linked to the organisation but not its own. phish.fi does not treat it as the organisation's domain, and a reporting address cannot be on it. |

### evidenceKind

Used by `domains[].evidenceKind` and `reportTo[].evidenceKind`.

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `official_site` | A page on the organisation's own website (the default). |
| `official_register` | An entry in an official register, such as a company register. For domains only; a reporting address cannot cite it. |
| `organisation_statement` | A public statement the organisation publishes or endorses outside its own website. |

### payload

Used by `reportTo[].payload`.

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `original_required` | Only send a report that includes the original message. |
| `original_preferred` | Include the original message when the reporter agrees; otherwise send the structured details. |
| `structured_only` | Send only the structured details (sender, links, findings), never the original message. |

### Alias kind

Used by `aliases[].kind`.

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `brand` | A brand or trading name. |
| `auth_product` | The name of an identification or sign-in product. |
| `app` | The name of a mobile or desktop app. |
| `service` | The name of a service the organisation offers. |
| `former_name` | A name the organisation used before. |

### Alias match

Used by `aliases[].match`.

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `token_exact` | The words of the name must appear exactly (the default). |
| `token_stem` | The last word of the name is a stem, so inflected forms also match ("Kela" matches "Kelalta"). The last word needs at least 4 characters. |

### Alias weight

Used by `aliases[].weight`.

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `low` | A weak hint: the name alone does not count as a sign that a message claims to be from the organisation. Use it for short or common names. |
| `medium` | A moderate hint: the name alone counts as a sign that a message claims to be from the organisation (the default for names longer than 4 characters). |
| `high` | A strong hint. It is never the default; use it only for a long, unmistakable name. |

### organisationType

Used by `organisationType`.

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `private_company` | A privately owned company. |
| `listed_company` | A company whose shares trade on a stock exchange. |
| `public_sector` | A government body or other public authority. |
| `non_profit` | A non-profit organisation, association or foundation. |
| `educational_institution` | A school, college or university. |
| `healthcare_provider` | A hospital, clinic or other provider of health care. |
| `international_organisation` | An organisation set up by several countries. |
| `other` | Anything else. |

### sector

Used by `sector` and `additionalSectors`.

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `financial_services` | Banks, insurance, payments and investment. |
| `healthcare_pharmaceuticals` | Health care and medicines. |
| `energy_utilities` | Electricity, gas, heating, water and similar utilities. |
| `telecommunications` | Telephone, mobile and internet services. |
| `government_public_administration` | Government and public administration. |
| `education_research` | Education and research. |
| `transport_logistics` | Transport, postal, parcel and delivery services. |
| `retail_ecommerce` | Shops and online stores. |
| `technology_software` | Technology and software. |
| `manufacturing_industry` | Manufacturing and industry. |
| `media_entertainment` | Media and entertainment. |
| `professional_services` | Consulting, legal, accounting and similar services. |
| `other` | Anything else. |

## Keys the maintainer sets

Leave these keys alone. Only the maintainer of the pack adds or changes them.
The check rejects a pull request that adds or changes `source`, `id`, `localizedNames`, `publicSourceUrl`, `scope`, `kind` or `notes`.
The maintainer reviews any change to `communicationPolicy`.
If one of these is wrong in an existing file, open an issue instead.

| Key | Needed | If you leave it out | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `domains[].source` | No | - | Maintainer only: the id of a source declared in pack.yaml, used in place of evidence, checked and says. |
| `reportTo[].source` | No | - | Maintainer only: the id of a source declared in pack.yaml, used in place of evidence, checked and says. |
| `reportTo[].localizedNames` | No | - | Maintainer only: the display name in other languages, keyed by language code. |
| `reportTo[].publicSourceUrl` | No | - | Maintainer only: the organisation's own https page that tells people to report to this address. Once the address is verified, phish.fi lists it publicly with a link to this page. |
| `reportTo[].scope` | No | - | Maintainer only: conditions that limit when this address is used. |
| `reportTo[].kind` | No | - | Maintainer only: organisation (the default) for the organisation's own address, or national for a CERT or authority, which needs scope. |
| `reportTo[].notes` | No | - | Maintainer only: notes for reviewers. |
| `reportTo[].id` | No | - | Maintainer only: keeps an existing destination id. Default: <organisation id>.<the address's local part>. |
| `communicationPolicy` | No | - | Maintainer only: what the organisation's emails never contain, from its published policy. |

### kind

Used by `reportTo[].kind`.

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `organisation` | The organisation's own address for reports about messages that imitate it (the default). |
| `national` | An address of a CERT or authority that takes reports about many organisations. It needs scope. |

### neverContains

Used by `communicationPolicy.neverContains`.

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `link_login` | A link to a sign-in page. |
| `link_identify` | A link that asks the person to identify themselves strongly, for example with online banking codes. |
| `link_payment` | A link to a payment page. |
| `link_credential_update` | A link to a page for updating credentials or account details. |
| `link_document_view` | A link to view a document. |
| `link_public_information` | A link to public information. |
| `link_unsubscribe` | A link to unsubscribe. |
| `link_unknown` | A link whose purpose is not known. |
